replacements.new:
Implement the complete replacement path. Return pre-activations as well as sparse features so later exercises can see which ReLU gates are open.

Before advancing, run this additional independent checkpoint in a new working-copy cell. It changes gate patterns, dimensions, decoder weights and biases; hard-coding the public red-square answer must fail. Work out the preactivations by hand before running it.

```python
x = t.tensor([[1.,0.],[0.,1.]])
E = t.tensor([[2.,-1.],[-1.,3.],[1.,1.]])
b = t.tensor([-1.,-2.,-.5])
D = t.tensor([[1.,2.],[-2.,1.],[.5,-1.]])
d = t.tensor([.25,-.5])
p, f = encode(x,E,b)
t.testing.assert_close(p,t.tensor([[1.,-3.,.5],[-2.,1.,.5]]))
t.testing.assert_close(f,t.tensor([[1.,0.,.5],[0.,1.,.5]]))
expected = t.tensor([[1.5,1.],[-1.5,0.]])
t.testing.assert_close(decode(f,D,d),expected)
y = transcoder_forward(x,E,D,encoder_bias=b,decoder_bias=d)
t.testing.assert_close(y.reconstructed_activations,expected)
```

For the later signed-path exercise, use the same tensors and readout `[1,-1]`: feature-to-score rows must be `[-1,0,.75]` and `[0,-3,.75]`, with input-plus-bias contributions summing to those rows. The decoder bias separately contributes `.75` to each total score (`.5` and `-1.5`); it must not be silently assigned to a sparse feature.
